medium_low_remediation_summary: Counted from self-reported counts in 73 unique fix-commit subject lines on dev (deduplicated from git log --all's 146, which double-counts every commit through both dev's original chain and its rebased-with-new-SHAs equivalent merged back in via PR #148's catch-up release) -- NOT independently cross-verified against original finding IDs in phase1_findings_scored.md / phase1_5_scored.md / phase2_findings_scored.md, because that cross-verification turned out not to be reliably possible: see numbering_scheme_finding below. Aggregate: 80 Medium fixed (of 99 reported -- matches the 0.18.0 CHANGELOG's "large majority of ~90 Medium findings" framing) and 1 Low fixed (of 70 reported -- consistent with Low-severity findings being largely deferred rather than actioned, as expected under normal severity-based prioritization, not a sign of incomplete bookkeeping). Critical and High findings from this same pass are already fully accounted for in kicad-mcp-20260923-7f3a's own "notes" field (45 fixed / 5 partial / 3 false-positive / 4 deferred, of 55) and are not restated here.
numbering_scheme_finding: Investigated whether fix-commit messages' "finding #N" numbers map to absolute position in the corresponding *_scored.md scratchpad file, to allow a fully itemized backfill (as kicad-mcp-remediate-20260924-b1cf did for the 2026-07-21 pass, where original findings WERE individually numbered in the ledger itself). Result: Phase 1.5's numbering DOES match absolute position in phase1_5_scored.md (confirmed by a peer session). Phase 1's does NOT: commit 8b56bfd ("Fix MEDIUM finding #24 from the 2026-09-23 full review (Phase 1)") actually fixes the pcb_footprints.py/pcb_keepout.py overhang-logic duplication, which is the 29th MEDIUM entry (not the 24th of any severity) in phase1_findings_scored.md, and falls under that file's "## Reuse / duplication" section rather than its main correctness list -- no tested position/section/severity-filtered scheme matched. Separately, many Phase 1 and Phase 2 fix commits do not use "finding #N" at all -- they identify their target by file/area name instead (e.g. "Fix 2 MEDIUM findings from the 2026-09-23 full review (bom.py Phase 1)"). Conclusion: no single consistent Phase 1 numbering scheme survived to reconstruct; the commit messages' own numbers most likely reflected an ad hoc triage ordering used live during that session and never written to any preserved file. Itemizing this backfill by original finding ID would therefore require fabricating a precision the source data does not actually have -- an aggregate count with this caveat stated plainly is more honest than a false-confident per-finding table.
